newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia stocks end strong on CRA, book-squaring.
newsitem.headline: Australia stocks end strong on CRA, book-squaring.

text.p: Australian stocks ended a shortened trading session stronger on Thursday, boosted by a two percent rally in miner RTZ Corp Plc-CRA Ltd, quarter-end book-squaring and a buoyant gold sector.
"It was strong, backed by the rise in CRA on this iron ore deal in the Pilbara," said broker David Massey at Eyres Reed.
CRA announced late on Wednesday it had struck a deal with local aborigines allowing its A$500 million Yandicoogina iron ore development in Western Australia to go ahead.
The All Ordinaries index closed up 18 points at 2,422.3 three hours earlier than normal ahead of the Easter break.

RTZ-CRA closed up 39 cents or 2.11 percent at A$18.86, dragging the All Resources Index up 0.88 percent, offsetting a late slide in BHP's share price after news it would struggle to cut its copper costs.
BHP closed up three cents at A$17.00, coming off a A$17.13 high in earlier trade when BHP Copper chief executive Jim Lewis said copper costs per pound were a high 80 cents.

NAB's 16 cent rise to A$16.15 helped boost the banking index 0.60 percent. Brokers said NAB continued its technical rebound from support found around A$15.50 this week after a sharp fall over the last month.
The major trade of the day was a crossing of 4.99 percent stake in John Fairfax Holdings Ltd at A$3.00 per share, which brokers said was Conrad Black selling his remaining stake.
Fairfax closed up 2.3 cents at A$3.103.

Gold stocks rose after the Comex Gold price jumped US$3.00 to US$353.50 on startling revelations by Freeport McMoran that Busang II tests showed insignificant amounts of gold at the Indonesian prospect.
Brokers also said local gold groups were likely to benefit from any foreign capital flight from Indonesia in the wake of controversy over the legitimacy of Busang resource estimates.
The gold index closed up 1.28 percent, driven by a three cent rise in Plutonic Resources to A$4.95 and a three cent rise in Normandy to A$1.73.
Strong performances from the gold stocks exposed to Papua New Guinea also helped the gold sector.

Papua New Guinea-linked stocks jumped in active early trade after PNG Prime Minister Julius Chan stood aside late on Wednesday to resolve 10 days of political turmoil in Port Moresby caused by the hiring of mercenaries.
Orogen Minerals Ltd, which is 51 percent owned by the PNG government, rose eight cents to A$3.10.
Lihir Gold Ltd closed up two cents at A$2.15 while Oil Search Ltd closed up 13 cents at A$2.70. Bougainville Copper closed up five cents at 60 cents.
In other markets, Australian bonds were also buoyed by quarter-end book-squaring and some overseas buying. The June 10 year bond future contract was up three point at 91.925 in afternoon trade.
The Australian dollar was holding its overnight gains at US$0.7865/70 in afternoon trade, supported by buying from a Japanese investment house and short-covering ahead of the Easter break.
